t: This is the Sondheim Theatre, on Shaftesbury Avenue at the corner of Wardour Street. It opened as the Queen's Theatre on 8 October 1907, a twin to the neighbouring Hicks Theatre, and both were designed by W. G. R. Sprague. He had been apprenticed to Frank Matcham and went on to design at least thirty-five theatres. The building has been Grade II listed since 1972. Today it carries the name of Stephen Sondheim, the American composer and lyricist who reinvented the American musical.
